column2: A building you've never been in. Room one-oh-four is somewhere upstairs.
And the one thing you'd normally reach for, stops working at the door.
This is Indoor Nav. Directions inside a building, with nothing but your phone.
It starts with a printed marker. Black and white squares, stuck at a known spot.
Point your camera at it, and the phone itself works out exactly where you are.
A corrected, bidirectional Dike-struh search finds the shortest way, through rooms, corridors, stairs and lifts.
Can't take the stairs? Step-free. Rather skip the lift? Avoid lifts.
And when your route changes floors,
you see exactly how you get there.
Lose your way? Scan any marker, and the route starts again from there.
And in beta: scan once, then just walk, with spoken turns.
It all works in airplane mode. No GPS. No Wi-Fi. No beacons. No server.
Set-up starts from the building's own floor plan. And the whole building shares as one file.
It used to take a microcontroller, Wi-Fi, and a cloud database.
Now it takes a phone, and a sticker.
So what could it do for a whole campus?
Indoor Nav. Find your way, anywhere indoors.
